definitions.explanation: The humble or formal term for one's own grandmother. Used when speaking about your grandmother to others in polite contexts.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{元気|げんき}です。
{祖母|そぼ}は{今年|ことし}{八十歳|はちじゅっさい}になります。
examples.english: My grandmother will turn 80 this year.

examples.japanese: {毎週|まいしゅう}{祖母|そぼ}に{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.english: I call my grandmother every week.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{遠|とお}くに{住|す}んでいますので、{夏休|なつやす}みによく{会|あ}いに{行|い}きます。
examples.english: My grandmother lives far away, so I often go to see her during summer vacation.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}の{祖母|そぼ}は{若|わか}い{時|とき}、{先生|せんせい}でした。{今|いま}でも{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのが{好|す}きです。
examples.english: My grandmother was a teacher when she was young. She still likes reading books.

notes: {祖母|そぼ} is the humble/formal term used when referring to your own grandmother in polite speech. In casual speech or when speaking directly to your grandmother, おばあさん or おばあちゃん is used. When referring to someone else's grandmother politely, use おばあさん or おばあさま.
